Why deja-vu Is Trending

The Backend landscape is constantly evolving, and deja-vu has emerged as one of the fastest-growing projects this week. Several factors contribute to its momentum:

  1. Growing community: With 11 new stars this week alone, developer adoption is accelerating rapidly.
  2. Active maintenance: The project sees regular updates, ensuring compatibility with the latest ecosystem changes.
  3. Practical utility: Your agents already solved this. deja finds it — retroactive search and MCP recall over the session logs your coding agents already wrote. Cross-agent, SSH-portable, one zero-dep binary, fully local.

If you're working in Backend, this is definitely a project worth watching — and adopting.

How It Compares to Alternatives

When evaluating deja-vu, it's natural to compare it against established alternatives. Here's what sets it apart:

  • Performance: Built with Go, it leverages modern language features for speed.
  • Community size: 397 stars indicate strong community trust and validation.
  • License: MIT licensing means no commercial restrictions.

Final Thoughts

deja-vu is a solid addition to any developer's toolkit. With its growing community, active development, and practical design, it's well worth your time to evaluate. Star it on GitHub, try it in a side project, and see if it fits your workflow.
